QUOTE: The high-level part is `ret & 0xFF80`. If it is nonzero, `mbedtls_high_level_strerr()` (`library/error.c:174`) looks it up. ... The low-level part is `ret & ~0xFF80`. If it is nonzero, `mbedtls_low_level_strerr()` (`library/error.c:537`) looks it up. If both parts are present, the strings are joined with `" : "`.
VERDICT: HIT
WHY: The answer describes the high-level and low-level parts of the code and says that `mbedtls_strerror` joins both strings with " : " when both are present.
